evals.prompt: You are a recruiter who has read thousands of resumes. Read docs/Julien-Clifford-Resume.pdf and give feedback.
evals.expected_output: Runs scripts/scan.sh on the PDF and renders the page before judging. Opens with a one-line verdict (lazy AI, edited by checklist, or human). Reports every finding, numbered, in three groups: hard problems, tells, what works, each quoting the line. Covers dates and tenure, the top entry, headline versus recent roles, extraction faults, pronoun 'it', article density, uniform rhythm, repeated facts, weighting, unverifiable numbers. Ends with one priority order. Does not rewrite the resume unasked and does not add facts.
assertions: Runs scan.sh and reads the extracted text
Renders the page and judges layout
Lists every finding with a severity, not a shortlist
Quotes the offending line for each finding
Names what works and should be kept
Gives one priority order after the full list
Does not invent facts or numbers

evals.prompt: Does this resume look AI-generated? 'Results-driven engineer with a proven track record of spearheading cross-functional initiatives. Leveraged cutting-edge technologies to drive innovation and improve operational efficiency. Responsible for high-impact features.'
evals.expected_output: Verdict: lazy AI. Flags every stock phrase (results-driven, proven track record, spearheading, cross-functional, leveraged, cutting-edge, drive innovation, operational efficiency, responsible for, high-impact). Flags that no line carries an outcome, a number, a product or a named thing. Points to CLAUDE.md writing rules for the rewrite and asks for the facts behind each claim rather than inventing them.
assertions: Flags absence of outcomes and named things
Asks for the underlying facts instead of inventing replacements

evals.prompt: Check that the resume PDF will parse. docs/Julien-Clifford-Resume.pdf
evals.expected_output: Runs scan.sh, reports letter-spaced runs (none or listed), font embedding (CID TrueType expected, Type 3 is a failure), reading order of the extracted text, and any glyphs that extract as garbage. If a fault exists, names the CSS cause (tracking on uppercase labels, variable fonts, tables) and the fix, then rebuilds and re-extracts to prove the fix.
assertions: Reports on font type and embedding
Names the CSS cause for any fault
